svg.title: Property Tax Appeal Odds-and-Leverage Funnel
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-property-tax-appeal-odds-funnel; chapter number: 6; title: Property Tax Appeal Odds-and-Leverage Funnel; subtitle: Deadline discipline, win rates, and the value levers that move assessments; chart type: funnel; stages: label: Timely Filing Gate; value: 100; display: Index 100; conversion: Entry: on-time filings only; detail: Miss the deadline by a single day and that year's assessment cannot be appealed (USA Senior Laws Guide); calendar every 30-day county change notice mid-appeal (Save Paulding).; label: Win or Partial Reduction Ceiling; value: 60; display: 60%; conversion: Up to 60% of homeowner appeals; detail: Wins mostly go to owners who gather specific evidence and show up (USA Senior Laws Guide).; label: Win or Partial Reduction Floor; value: 30; display: 30%; conversion: At least 30% in most counties; detail: Roy requests that the appraiser present first; in one Douglas County hearing the board cut land from $32,000 to $12,000 an acre (Save Paulding).; label: Cap-Rate Value Lever; value: 20; display: ~20% value per 1% cap-rate move; conversion: Income-approach swing on commercial assets; detail: Wes Nichols flags owners who recently bought at very low cap rates as prime review targets for tax years 23 and 24 (Paramount Property Tax Appeal).; label: Hotel Intangible Strip Floor; value: 15; display: 15% to 20% off purchase price; conversion: Goodwill removed from newly acquired hotels; detail: Assessors fail to strip intangible and goodwill value when they work the sale (Paramount Property Tax Appeal).; caption: A property tax appeal is a fight over assessed value, never the bill. Contingency fees run 25% to 50% of savings; George Evers's 35% worked example earns $84,000, and Eric Nelson reports a $900,000 reduction that returned $12,900 more to the client.; assumptions note: Stage 1 is indexed to 100 for scale. Stages 2 and 3 are the reported 30%-60% homeowner win-or-partial band; stages 4 and 5 are commercial value levers on a percent scale, not a share of filings. Big wins can invite county counter-appeals: Save Paulding saw 6 of 18 same-day properties taken to court.; note: Attributed to USA Senior Laws Guide (LopTSxbolHY), Save Paulding (oIIj8lWBYVY), Paramount Property Tax Appeal (fOMz56wkRgs, R_juWiwAZ-k), Cross the River, Find the Treasure (7CfK4x3Fijc), and Eric Nelson (APAYRO4lrsk).

rect.title: label: Timely Filing Gate; value: 100; display: Index 100; conversion: Entry: on-time filings only; detail: Miss the deadline by a single day and that year's assessment cannot be appealed (USA Senior Laws Guide); calendar every 30-day county change notice mid-appeal (Save Paulding).

label: Win or Partial Reduction Ceiling; value: 60; display: 60%; conversion: Up to 60% of homeowner appeals; detail: Wins mostly go to owners who gather specific evidence and show up (USA Senior Laws Guide).

label: Win or Partial Reduction Floor; value: 30; display: 30%; conversion: At least 30% in most counties; detail: Roy requests that the appraiser present first; in one Douglas County hearing the board cut land from $32,000 to $12,000 an acre (Save Paulding).

label: Cap-Rate Value Lever; value: 20; display: ~20% value per 1% cap-rate move; conversion: Income-approach swing on commercial assets; detail: Wes Nichols flags owners who recently bought at very low cap rates as prime review targets for tax years 23 and 24 (Paramount Property Tax Appeal).

label: Hotel Intangible Strip Floor; value: 15; display: 15% to 20% off purchase price; conversion: Goodwill removed from newly acquired hotels; detail: Assessors fail to strip intangible and goodwill value when they work the sale (Paramount Property Tax Appeal).

text.title: Assumptions: Stage 1 is indexed to 100 for scale. Stages 2 and 3 are the reported 30%-60% homeowner win-or-partial band; stages 4 and 5 are commercial value levers on a percent scale, not a share of filings. Big wins can invite county counter-appeals: Save Paulding saw 6 of 18 same-day properties taken to court.
